patch.value: Generation lineage: a policy generation is an item whose parent is the generation that produced its training data

A Generation records the base checkpoint it started from, the policy that collected its training data, the Run ids of those collection episodes, and the training configuration that turned them into a successor. Its parent edge points at the generation whose policy did the collecting. Which generation produced this trajectory then stops being a question answered by a filename convention and becomes a reachability query over edges pm already stores and merges losslessly. The edge also carries the invalidation frontier for free: an environment edit reaches every descendant without pm-rl maintaining a second index of its own.

A generation with no parent is accepted as the seed generation and reports itself as such; every later generation requires a parent that exists and is itself promoted; the collection runs named by a generation must reference the parent's policy and are refused when they do not; the recorded checkpoint identity is content-addressed so a silently swapped checkpoint fails to resolve

patch.value: A generation with no parent is accepted as the seed generation and reports itself as such; every later generation requires a parent that exists and is itself promoted; the collection runs named by a generation must reference the parent's policy and are refused when they do not; the recorded base checkpoint, environment version and reward-spec version identities are content-addressed so a silently swapped artifact fails to resolve; an edit to an environment or reward specification is reachable in reverse to every generation whose collection runs used it, transitively through the parent chain; the declared edge types are enumerated in the specification rather than inferred

A Generation records the base checkpoint it started from, the policy that collected its training data, the Run ids of those collection episodes, and the training configuration that turned them into a successor. Its parent edge points at the generation whose policy did the collecting. Which generation produced this trajectory then stops being a question answered by a filename convention and becomes a reachability query over edges pm already stores and merges losslessly. The parent edge alone is not sufficient, and assuming otherwise was the gap in the first draft of this specification. A parent edge connects a generation to its predecessor; it does not connect an environment revision or a reward specification to the generations that used it, so reverse reachability from an environment edit reaches nothing. A generation therefore declares typed edges to the exact environment version and reward-spec version each of its collection runs used, in addition to the parent edge and the collection-run edges. Every one of those references is content-addressed, so a silently swapped artifact fails to resolve rather than resolving to something else. Invalidation is then the reverse traversal of those edges and needs no second index.

message: Require environment and reward-spec edges so reverse reachability can implement invalidation
